## 2026-11-19: program-owned generic registries and leased compiler sessions

Pulled current main before work. The user prioritizes explicit world ownership
alongside the full language roadmap. Module-scoped bindings/aliases remain the
next language visibility slice; first retire two concrete ownership hazards in
the real compiler. GenericContext currently obtains four process-lifetime type
entities from compiler-syntax.cpp. Move that registry into Tower: each program's
context component owns its type entity, which owns the other generic component
types. Existing entity/component references reclaim the registry naturally; no
new collector, native callback, global current-world selector or semantic IR.
Delete the superseded native registry/component adapter once replaced.

ModuleEnvironment currently lends the same mutable compilation session to every
module graph, resetting a still-active request when another starts. Give each
module an exclusive session lease; its environment owns at most one idle cached
session. Repeated acquisition by the same module is idempotent. Resetting cached
grammar state retires a generation, never destroys a live lease; obsolete leases
are destroyed when their module graph drains. Refuse world/environment disposal
while request graphs remain live. This keeps parser-table reuse for serial builds
and allows independent interleaved requests without a global current session.

These are coordinator-owned lifetime changes, not a claim of threaded mutation:
native parser/Foundation registries, grammar baselines, source/diagnostic
publication and the singleton entity store still require migration. Validate
independent generic identities/lifetime, interleaved parse continuations, reset
while leased, reuse, teardown, language queries, compiler successors and overhead
before publication. Implement algorithms and functional assertions in Tower;
native edits only remove the replaced code. Journal outcomes and remaining
dependencies below.

Implemented compiler/generic-registry.tower and removed the native four-type
registry plus component-add wrapper from compiler-syntax.cpp (seven deleted
lines, no native additions). Each program's context component retains its registry
type, whose child entities own template/instance/origin types; attached components
independently retain their types. The Tower fixture verifies different programs in
one store, another store, cross-registry lookup, a component outliving its context,
no phantom program children, and repeated complete reclamation. Both pointer
widths, graph/fast execution, Foundation round trips, raw/optimized reconstruction
and Wasm execution pass (ownership-registry-fixture.log, 4/4).

Compilation sessions now belong exclusively to their module until its graph
drains. Reacquiring the same module is idempotent; another active module receives
another parser. The environment caches one returned session. Reset increments a
cache generation and disposes only idle state; active sessions continue, and
retired ones are destroyed on return. frontend_modules_try_destroy rejects live
request graphs. Native SyntaxSession storage and global grammar baselines remain;
input changes, diagnostics and lease bookkeeping are still coordinator-owned.
This is not full native-world isolation or concurrent environment mutation.

The first build exposed the still-flat module namespace: adding a second abort
extern collided with host-entities. Moved the shared declaration/infallible
compiler check into entity-require.tower and imported it from both owners.
Recoverable entity-library allocation failures retain their existing return
contract. The sanitizer cache initially pointed at an obsolete stage1 compiler
that rejects --depfile; reconfigured it with the existing import-capable bootstrap
at build/import-port/towerc. An initial direct test launch from the repository
root could not find bedrock.tower; using the established CTest working directory
fixes the invocation. No compiler behavior was changed for either setup failure.

Native compiler/backend API checks pass. The native parser suite, including the
new Tower interleaving/reset/reuse/disposal assertions, passes in 193.10 seconds
with address/undefined sanitizers on its native code (ownership-parser-tests.log;
ctest --test-dir /home/trevo/.cache/tower/core-asan -R '^tower-parser-tests$'
--output-on-failure). Canonical formatting passes. Rebuilt parser/LLVM/cross
reactors; the complete Node/Wasm suite passes 341/341 in 61.79 seconds. That run
overlapped packaging, so repeated the five compiler-worker checks after the new
recipe finished; all pass. Successor builds below validate the new recipe itself.

## 2026-11-20: remove native provenance and generic metadata ownership

Pulled d8d856c on clean main. Continue from 6,534 production native lines in 55
files. Move SyntaxOrigin and immutable expansion history into Tower components
on the same world/entity model, then retire compiler-syntax.cpp's name collection
and metadata copying. Keep captured/generated spans, previous chains, splices,
session-independent lifetime and browser JSON stable. Native edits only remove
implementations or mechanically connect existing transport/declarations to Tower
payloads; no new native wrapper/test/fallback. Expansion traversal already lives
in Tower and will own its temporary trace references there. Test self/cross-world
copying, failed allocations, deep history reclamation, reset survival and visible
provenance. Preserve pinned metadata until views drain. Rebuild native/browser,
compare raw/optimized behavior and compiler successors, benchmark the saved
pre-change LLVM reactor, then publish and verify. Baseline saved in
build/language-next/provenance-baseline/tower-llvm.wasm.

Implemented provenance as CompilerSyntaxOrigin and CompilerSyntaxExpansion entity
components in syntax-provenance.tower. Histories own their rule text and retain
previous traces; origins retain primary/splice traces. Copying prepares all
fallible storage before replacing destination metadata. Reclamation detaches
unique unpinned predecessor links iteratively; pinned owners defer destruction
until the coordinator closes the view. Refcounts remain coordinator-owned, not
atomic worker mutation. The world API is independent of native sessions and
transport; host-provenance.tower only selects the legacy default world. That host
pre-registers the two provenance identities to preserve allocation-baseline
behavior. Explicit worlds remain lazy. The existing Tower expander now owns and
releases its temporary traces on success and failure.

Removed compiler-syntax.cpp and the native sem_match definition. Tower metadata
access follows shared parser components, compares ordinary single-terminal names
without allocation, and uses the existing Tower identifier decoder for quoted or
composite names. Metadata copies retain provenance independently of the source.
Browser changes only borrow the new payload layout; JSON fields and trace
identity/order are unchanged. No Foundation grammar change, native implementation,
wrapper, functional test or fallback seed was added.

New Tower assertions cover world rejection, spans, copied rule text, shared history
with independent splice storage, self-copy, failed allocations preserving existing
state, source destruction, a 10,000-entry predecessor chain, pinned lifetime and
reclamation, plain/quoted/composite names, and generic metadata copying. Existing
native syntax tests retain generated trees after destroying their sessions.

## 2026-11-20: Inspect matched custom syntax and simplify grammar hovers

The follow-up screenshots exposed two presentation errors and a coverage gap:
import path terms emitted `category` before being reclassified as module imports;
alternative previews inserted hard newlines and a redundant active-alternative
count; ordinary custom-rule matches had neither grammar-declaration components
nor checked Foundation values, so the hover eligibility filter hid every token
of `examples/foreach.tower`'s nested loop. Prior full Bedrock/Foundation and
replacement-tree tests did not exercise this syntax-only body path.

Tower document queries now retain the actual source alternative for each ordinary
matched production while its parser version is current. A narrow read-only native
bridge maps the match's production index and label through the existing derived
Version index to its shared source entity. Tower owns retention, traversal,
classification, documentation, canonical previews, and JSON emission. Generated
capture/repetition productions are flattened by `lr-tree.tower`; capture identity
therefore follows the actual named ECS child relationships to the source terms,
not guessed token spelling or generated rule names. The query builds a disposable
entity-keyed SemanticTable index after parsing instead of repeatedly scanning its
snapshot vector. Source alternatives remain correct across later `=` overrides.

When ordinary semantic checking is unavailable, source tokens now explain the
matched rule, selected production, named capture/owner, source location, and
attached comments. These are grammar facts, not invented runtime types; existing
successfully checked programs keep their typed binding hovers. Syntax-only
examples and erroneous programs explicitly report that no resolved runtime type
is available. Import hovers expose the module name and import role before the
grammar-term path can emit a category. Alternative previews share the existing
formatter and use ` | ` with natural wrapping. The frontend removes the active
alternative count and avoids repeating identical matched-rule/category fields.
The existing preview opacity, dwell, five-pixel tolerance, retargeting, and cached
mouse path are unchanged.

Added regression coverage for every token of the exact nested foreach example,
later redefinition, named terminal captures, imported rules selecting Number versus
Identifier, import categorization, memory reclamation, and desktop/mobile rendered
hover content without hover-time worker requests. Compiler successor activation
now also probes syntax-only captures and module import metadata. Initial build
trials caught Tower's unsupported by-value struct call and required explicit
pointer conversion; corrected the scratch vector append to the project's existing
reserve/copy pattern. The first mobile browser trial hovered an offscreen line
after inserting the full example; scrolling each target line into view fixed the
test, and both device profiles passed the exact example.

Environment: Windows PowerShell, WSL Orchestral-Revng, WASI SDK 34, main at
`d8d856c` before this change. Rebuilt parser and LLVM/cross reactors through
`build/context-bootstrap.sh` and the established `build-wasm.sh` / `build-llvm.sh`
scripts (`TOWER_BROWSER_CROSS=ON`), then rebuilt the full static distribution with
`TOWER_REQUIRE_BACKENDS=1`. Logs are ignored `build/hover-followup-*.log`.

desktop/mobile. The 28 focused query tests include all earlier typed/grammar/

## 2026-11-20: Plain language and compact capture hovers

Follow-up UX requests supersede the previous explanatory wording: `=` describes
setting how to write this part of the language, replacing any earlier version;
`|=` describes adding another way. Both explicitly apply to the code below.
Matched source nodes now say "This code matches the pattern shown below." The
query still reports only actual grammar facts when semantic checking has no
resolved value type; removing the technical disclaimer does not invent types.

The renderer combines capture name, category, and owning rule in one line, e.g.
`Capture: $value:Expression in ForEach`. An implicit capture named for its category
does not repeat that category. A matched-rule row remains only when there is no
capture or its actual nested rule differs from the capture category. This matters
for `Outer = Inner`: the named capture can accept Outer while the most specific
matched subtree is Inner. Generic "matched syntax" and "captured syntax" labels
are hidden; query metadata and meaningful binding/type information are retained.

Removed the obsolete implementation comment from foreach and rewrote its other
comments around the example's behavior. Removed explicit language-name references
from project-owned Tower comments exposed in builtins/compiler source, emitted
C comments, and diagnostic prose. ABI spellings and third-party license notices
remain intact. A narrowly anchored startup migration removes the exact retired
comment from saved foreach.tower files without changing their other text, so
existing browser workspaces receive the requested cleanup after reload.

tooltip overlap option prevents collision avoidance from moving this bubble away
from its pointer anchor. Viewport clamping and above/below placement remain active.

dismissal margin and delayed switching to neighboring symbols are unchanged.

## 2026-11-20: Tree-based IDE services and consistent source locations

The user requested compact function hovers, consistent source locations, and
queries for keywords, operators and delimiters rather than name-only coverage.
They explicitly requested reusable Tower compiler services, shared by IDE clients.
Added compiler/services.tower as the actual imported library entry module used by
ComposeSemanticSources.cmake. It collects the existing checking, completion,
inspection, source metadata and formatting implementation modules; this is a
working import boundary, not a separate parser, AST, semantic model or server.
docs/compiler-services.md records direct query entry points, handle ownership,
UTF-8 offsets, explicit pointer-width inputs and remaining native adapters.

The root cause of missing keyword hovers was that language_candidate narrowed a
declaration/call to its name. Tower's new language_context_candidate follows the
same leaf's parent relationships to its nearest checked Foundation operation.
It distinguishes declaration/initialization, assignment destinations, pointer
read/write, return, function parameter/body boundaries and structural control
flow. Function closing braces identify their actual containing function. Values
use checked types and canonical signatures; blocks/if/loop/break/continue have
descriptions without fabricated runtime types. Literal spelling only refines an
already selected operation's role. The browser still performs interval hit-tests
and presentation only, with no hover-time compiler request.

Review found that an uninstantiated generic call statement has no Foundation
payload. The initial parent walk could revisit that statement through its call
child; it now descends to the call only when its semantic payload exists. Actual
matched-production metadata is retained even after successful checking, but is
displayed only when no semantic subject was selected. Thus uninstantiated bodies
retain tree lookups without pretending to have concrete types.

Function tooltips omit the duplicate function and Returns rows while preserving
Result byte size/alignment. Source positions use filename.tower:line:column in
hover definitions/declarations, cursor status, inline errors and their shortcut,
and grammar diagnostic references. The Tower module service now exports
frontend_module_location; it uses the same immutable SyntaxSource position helper
as grammar locations and handles imported declarations in their actual file.
The browser shares one location renderer and counts Unicode scalars consistently
with Tower instead of UTF-16 units. Switching/restoring editor state explicitly
updates the cursor label. Cross-file diagnostics use the corresponding source.

An initial reuse of driver_source_position produced an unresolved env import in
the browser reactor: that driver-only helper is not linked into this target.
Replaced it with the existing syntax-source position logic through the Tower
module API, rather than introducing a JS import or a native implementation.
The first native diagnostic-text edit also exposed CoreName's string overload:
used string separators rather than a char for its first concatenation. Updated
the diagnostic/browser expectations to the shared location spelling.

## 2026-11-20: Generic ECS dispatch for language inspection

The user clarified that keywords/operators must not gain individual hover cases:
source lookup should be generic, with component-specific formatting allowed.
The prior language_context_candidate did walk actual parents, but also compared
literal token spellings and selected a list of operation kinds. Removed that
separate fallback and the operation allow-list. language_candidate now enumerates
each entity's actual components during the same tree walk. Presentation dispatch
in language-components.tower has explicit priority (Foundation, grammar, parsed
annotations/specializations), independent of component storage order. Whole
semantic node spans supply coverage; descendants provide more specific metadata.
Foundation operation descriptions/binding projections remain presentation code,
using operation tags and actual semantic relationships, never source token text.
Both ends of a block now present the same block information. Canonical signatures,
resolved layouts, attached comments and source locations retain their existing
formatting/ownership. The browser's synchronous cached lookup is unchanged.

Added a regression that changes declarations to let, assignment/initialization to
:=, return to give, statement terminators to !, and function headers to procedure
with [] and ->. Every non-whitespace position in its executable source has useful
inspection data; declaration punctuation shares the declaration entity and type.
The first test also changed block braces to begin/end, but ordinary semantic
checking correctly rejected that unsupported CoreBlock shape. Kept the compiler
contract unchanged and tested custom function-header punctuation instead. This is
a test-fixture correction, not a new promise that arbitrary Foundation shapes
are legal without Tower replacements.

Full-span inheritance exposed a separate correctness concern: a generic function's
specialization preview must not supply a concrete type to its uninstantiated source
body. The parsed-component presenter scopes that preview to the declaration name;
the body keeps matched-rule/capture metadata. A regression instantiates the same
function with both i32 and bool and checks the distinct calls plus untyped source
body. Resolved ordinary functions skip the specialization search entirely.

Built through the published Tower/Wasm bootstrap using WSL/WASI SDK 34. The initial
full Node/Wasm suite passed 358/358 (generic-hover-all-tests.log); after the generic
preview guard, focused hover checks pass 33/33 (generic-hover-tests.log). No native
compiler changes were required. Compared whole document inspection against the

Architecture: Tower-written roku-emitter.tower consumes checked FoundationNode
entities after the existing scalar LLVM optimization/reconstruction path. O0
still uses this bridge with passes disabled. The emitter shares the C emitter's
disposable entity/owner index and text helpers, without reading its generated C
or the private fast instruction cache. CLI --target roku / --emit brightscript
and browser Roku BrightScript selection emit a self-contained source file.
Each source target resolves its own layout before optimization; Roku uses four
byte little-endian addresses, C retains its eight-byte browser profile. Existing
worker cancellation/revision checks govern the new output and download lifetime.
No new Foundation operation, semantic graph, or program interchange is introduced.

Runtime design: exact LongInteger bit patterns, 16-bit limb arithmetic,
unsigned restoring division, signed overflow/zero traps, bool/range conversions,
byte-address memory, per-call frames, reusable/coalesced allocations, raw
load/store, overlap-safe copy, fill, recursion and ordinary calls. Argument and
temporary arrays avoid BrightScript's small variable and argument tables. The
complete-program entry is TowerRun; native foreign calls are diagnosed except
for the explicit platform_write text adapter. Conservative diagnostics enforce
240 labels / 200 conditionals per function and 1.9 MB / 60,000 lines per source.
These limits follow wasm2brs's device observations; they are not new Tower
language limits. Auto splitting and a general BrightScript import/export ABI are
future work. Default memory resource limit is 64 MiB. VM range containment is
separate from the raw Foundation pointer contract; no checked object handles or
lifetime generations are stored in pointers.

1. Native generation built with the existing /cache/performance-bootstrap/towerc

   import names; corrected those names. Bool bitwise AND is not a Foundation
   integer operation; replaced two index predicates with ordinary conditions.
2. Installed pinned brs-node 2.7.1 / BrighterScript 0.73.8 as test dependencies.
   Node 21 cannot run the simulator (Iterator.values().map unavailable); use
   Node 22.23.5 via `npm exec --yes --package=node@22 -- node ...` locally.

   createPayloadFromFileMap/executeFile API, with captured streams and no device
   network discovery; this removes that CLI-specific nuisance entirely.
3. A direct LongInteger `1& << 32` trial failed with Invalid Bitwise Shift;
   `1& << 31` produced a signed 32-bit value. Native wide shifts cannot be an
   assumption. A first replacement using full-width integer division also
   rounded a masked 63-bit maximum in the simulator. Rejected that approach.
   Final helpers extract only masked 16-bit limbs with exactly representable
   Double scaling by powers of two, then rebuild using bounded LongInteger
   multiplication/bitwise OR. General arithmetic never converts a complete
   64-bit pattern to Float/Double. Small-divisor division operates on bounded
   chunks; full unsigned division uses exact restoring steps.
4. The byte-array trial loaded zero after writing a computed LongInteger byte;
   assigning an explicit Integer byte% before the store fixed it. Runtime
   stores/fills now make the byte conversion explicit. Probe files/logs remain
   under build/roku-{probe,smoke,debug}*. The first bool print used storage width
   8 and printed 1; emitter now identifies bool semantically and sends width 1
   to conversion/printing helpers, while actual storage remains one byte.
5. The first browser rebuild used an old bootstrap that did not accept --depfile.
   Reconfigured /cache/fast-browser with the validated performance bootstrap.

unresolved/conflicting grammars, allocation failure and cleanup, plus the existing
native/browser diagnostic and compiler self-build checks.

## 2026-11-20: Explain hover concepts instead of repeating their names

The user first rejected redundant captions such as "Defines this function," then
clarified that short novice explanations would be useful, especially explaining
that a mutable variable's value can change. Replaced the Foundation presenter's
label-like sentences with plain-language explanations of functions, variables,
parameters, fields, calls, assignment, pointers, return, blocks and control flow.
Function descriptions read checked parameter count and return type: no-input
functions say so, void means no returned value, and void pointers still return a
value. Shared declaration descriptions follow resolved bindings as well, so
variable/parameter/field references receive the same explanation as declarations.

remain distinct from these concept explanations. Updated existing query/browser
assertions, including function input/result variants and descriptions reached
through bindings. The Tower formatter ran successfully on the changed presenter.

in AGENTS.md, foundation docs, the journal and todo.txt remain outside this commit.

Implemented the first scope/alias path in Tower: per-program module ownership
and resolved import relationships are components on retained parse entities;
lookup tables use name plus module identity. Open imports contribute declarations
only to their importing module; aliases select an explicit module. Functions,
types, globals and template resolution consume these same scopes. Colliding
module-local names serialize to unique escaped Foundation identifiers. Existing
lexical locals and declaration forward references remain in the ordinary checker.
Import syntax and formatting retain optional aliases for dotted and quoted paths.
Core calls and types accept qualified names through ordinary grammar rules.

The compiler's existing source split contains mutually dependent declaration
helpers. Added declaration-only import cycles to migrate that code without
inventing shared global namespaces or hiding dependencies in host build order.
Cycles containing grammar declarations or initialization effects are rejected;
acyclic effects retain dependency-first, once-only order. Self imports remain
errors. Module loading still uses each file's immutable baseline and ordinary
incremental grammar updates. Explicit foreign declarations retain their separate
link-symbol contract: compatible declarations coalesce, and a matching Tower
export supplies their implementation. Incompatible declarations and duplicate
exports diagnose instead of silently selecting an implementation.

Migrated 102 compiler/library/host/backend files to explicit imports, using an

validation. No runtime resolver scrapes source with that script. Platform-selected

modules and exported implementations selected by the existing build manifests.
The migrated native compiler rebuild completed with scope checking enabled.
This remains the existing hybrid compiler; these changes do not retire all native
adapters or claim a standalone distribution.

and fast interpreters, a canonical Foundation round trip, raw/optimized C compiled

## 2026-11-20: Tower native CLI host-policy migration

Pulled main from 04b0613 to 4ece094 before editing. The user assigned driver.cpp,
scaffolding/host/driver-*.tower, Tower CLI tests and an isolated build fragment,
with no new C++ implementation or tests and no uncoordinated compiler/backend API
changes. No subagents were used. todo.txt is untouched.

Implemented Tower ownership of option-result reporting and Roku output policy,
module-aware diagnostic composition through the existing frontend location API,
locale-independent ordered timing reports, optional LLVM output writes, owned
argument vectors, runtime compile/link command construction, temporary-file
lifetime and direct process execution. Tower's existing vector/ByteBuffer modules,
ordinary inferred locals, match and while are used; no alternate compiler graph
or instruction ABI was added. C++ changes are private host declarations and
connections to these Tower functions. The existing compilation, optimization,
packaging and interpreter entry APIs have not changed.

POSIX uses an explicit PATH search, fork/execv and a close-on-exec error pipe;
execv deliberately avoids execvp's implicit shell fallback for executable text
without a shebang. Windows uses the existing CRT _spawnvp ABI with Tower-written
Microsoft CRT argument quoting, including empty strings, embedded quotes and
trailing backslashes. Both preserve argument boundaries. Temporary creation uses
mkstemp or GetTempFileNameA, closes handles before tool execution and removes every
successfully created file on ordinary success/failure returns. Allocation failure
before creation cannot mark a path as owned. No shell interprets user arguments.
Supported host ABI profiles are explicit 64-bit Linux, macOS and Windows; this
does not constrain the compiler's output target or its 32-bit guest layouts.

Tower timing values are integer nanoseconds rendered as milliseconds with six
fractional digits in the existing sorted-key JSON envelope. Clock values only
measure host execution; they do not affect compiler semantics or cache identity.
The existing backend transport still supplies its double millisecond substage
measurements; the C++ connection converts their units at the boundary. Diagnostic
writes flush prior libc/iostream output before direct stream writes.

cmake/TowerDriver.cmake builds a separate production object, adds it to the native
CLI and retained stage1 target, and optionally builds standalone Tower tests.
The test executable reuses the existing runtime.c allocation/trap implementation;
it introduces no native test code. Test code is excluded from the production
object. The old TOWER_BOOTSTRAP_HOST implementations remain conditional seed code:
this turn does not establish a source-only bootstrap or justify deleting them.
Source compilation/grammar installation, CoreProgram and CoreMachine transport
still require the existing native interfaces. A complete orchestration port must
coordinate those API/lifetime boundaries with their owners; none was silently
changed or copied into a new driver semantic model.

Validation environment: Windows host plus the existing tower-c-validation Docker
container (tower_build, /work bind mount, /cache volume), LLVM 19, validated
/cache/performance-bootstrap/towerc. Default WSL is docker-desktop and has no bash;
used the existing build container instead. Native configuration:
cmake -S /work -B /cache/c-native -DTOWER_NATIVE=ON
-DTOWER_BOOTSTRAP_COMPILER=/cache/performance-bootstrap/towerc
-DCMAKE_PROJECT_scaffolding_INCLUDE=/work/cmake/TowerBackend.cmake
-DLLVM_DIR=/usr/lib/llvm-19/lib/cmake/llvm -DTOWER_DRIVER_TESTS=ON.
Build towerc and tower-driver-tests, then
ctest --test-dir /cache/c-native -R tower-driver --output-on-failure.
The full Tower CLI suite passes, covering exact captured stdout/errors, UTF-8

Review of upstream LLVM Unix/Path.inc confirmed TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP/TEMPDIR priority;
the Tower host now preserves that order and the empty-directory/current-directory
case. The no-environment POSIX fallback is /tmp; macOS normally supplies TMPDIR,
but the native per-user confstr fallback is not yet ported. Tests establish actual
Linux and Windows execution, not macOS runtime parity. Final validation and
publication evidence are recorded in the following entry.

A final ABI review found that declaring fcntl as a fixed-signature function is
not valid for Apple ARM64's variadic argument convention. Superseding the earlier
shared POSIX process implementation: Linux now uses fixed-signature pipe2 with
O_CLOEXEC and fork/execv; macOS uses fixed-signature posix_spawn with the exact
borrowed libc environment from _NSGetEnviron. This removes the variadic boundary
rather than adding a native shim. Shared PATH search, status normalization, file
ownership and diagnostics are unchanged. Linux's error pipe is now atomically
close-on-exec. The Tower CLI suite and macOS object compilation are rerun after
this correction; macOS runtime validation remains unavailable.

## 2026-11-20 — Symbolic template inspection on shared entities

Request: make generic/type-function definitions useful to inspect before an
instance exists, and use Tower constants/enums for inspection policy. Pulled
main before editing; unrelated AGENTS.md, foundation docs, journal additions and
todo.txt remain preserved and unstaged.

Root cause: generic definitions already carry registry metadata, but hover only
presented Foundation, grammar and parsed-type components. Its CoreFunction
fallback selected the first checked runtime function instance, so type-producing
functions were missed entirely and definition previews depended on unrelated
instantiation order. Removed that preview. `semantic-generic-info.tower` now
provides optional bounded source analysis, attaching GenericInfo components to
the actual definition/parameter/field/type-expression/reference entities. These
retain declaration bindings and the original annotation trees, reusing semantic
scope tables and ordinary resolution for independent types. Type/value inputs
remain symbolic, including nested applications, pointer/array annotations and
lexical shadowing. A type application's integer argument binds to its compile-time
value parameter even when parsed through CoreTypeName. Concrete instances still
receive the ordinary checker and target layouts; no generic-body type is borrowed
from the first instance. Budget/depth exhaustion marks the query incomplete.

The GenericInfo presenter uses the same component-dispatched tree walk and cached
document index. Canonical signature/type fragments use format-dependent.tower in
the existing formatting engine. The module API exposes borrowed paired lexer
comment spans so generic docs use the same comment normalization without browser
parsing or forced instantiation. GenericInfoKind and LanguagePresentation are
enums; depth/node/source/preview limits and trivia bytes are named Tower constants.
This is not full dependent-expression inference or whole-body checking before
instantiation. Unsupported body expressions still depend on ordinary checking.

Trials: the first build used the previous published compiler and rejected the
new upstream module cycles. After that process ended, pulled gh-pages a6bacaf
and used its scope-capable Tower/Wasm compiler through context-bootstrap.sh.
Initial new source used unsupported inline comparison conditions; lowered them
to ordinary Tower locals without extending the language grammar. Importing the
frontend implementation directly into the semantic link unit caused incompatible
foreign declaration types; replaced that dependency with the narrow borrowed
comment-span accessor. The query fixture initially targeted 'buffer' inside its
comment and expected noncanonical comma spacing; corrected those offsets/expected
formatting while retaining the semantic assertions.

format_same_tree replaces recursive native formatting verification with an
iterative Tower traversal. It queries the existing syntax and parser-match ECS
components and delegates grammar identity to syntax_nodes_equal. There is no
second AST or grammar model. Explicit component kinds and borrowed source ranges
keep inputs world-specific; work lists and output buffers are invocation-local.
Production context lookup uses sorted derived rows and binary search; detecting
one rule/multiple alternatives needs no temporary set/map allocations. Allocation
failure rejects an unverified formatting change. These are read-phase boundaries,
not a claim that shared entity-query caches or revision/session ownership are
already safe for within-unit parallel mutation. Unit compilation remains the
verified parallel path; pinning/world ownership still precedes phase scheduling.

## 2026-11-20: Runtime/allocator glue port and backend handoff

Started on clean main with `git pull --rebase`, advancing e2ae5ba to 894f903.
Read AGENTS.md, recent publication/fast-iteration entries, runtime.c,
compiler-memory.cpp, the existing Tower memory/output modules and the actual
Tower backend declaration/lowering path. No agents were spawned; todo.txt,
parser/syntax, browser transport and CLI policy are untouched. The user's ECS
follow-up applies to shared syntax/semantic entities and explicit context
ownership; pure allocator functions remain raw-storage functions. This work
makes no new parallel-execution or lock-free claim.

The host allocation policy was already Tower. Its last libc forwarding calls
now also live in Tower: memory-libc.tower declares the ordinary Foundation
foreign names `c_name(void* realloc(void*, size_t))` and
`c_name(void free(void*))`, with explicit lowered signatures
`(void*, usize): void*` and `(void*): void`. memory.tower defines the existing
compiler_host_reallocate/deallocate exports and compiler-memory.cpp deletes
its two C++ definitions. The production host unit imports these definitions
through its existing manifest and dependency file; no separate native shim or
new support archive was introduced. Foundation allocation count/size overflow,
zero-size release, optional diagnostics, failure-injection order and buffer
counters remain the existing Tower policy. Upstream libc still supplies storage
and target alignment; usize follows the selected target, never C++ host sizeof.

A rejected first attempt used qualified module calls to ordinary extern realloc
and free. Semantic declaration checking correctly rejects those builtin names
before qualified call resolution. The existing foreign-name identifiers solve
this without a grammar/backend edit. LLVM can optimize realloc(null,n) into
malloc; the host dependency allowlist now names malloc/realloc/free instead of
the deleted C bridges. The low-level exports remain available with their old ABI.

Correction to the earlier 2026-11-19 runtime handoff: this backend can already
lower explicit LLVM Wasm intrinsic declarations through ordinary foreign calls.
A Tower probe declaring `llvm.wasm.memory.size.i32(memory:u32):u32` and
`llvm.wasm.memory.grow.i32(memory:u32,pages:u32):u32` compiled and linked without
native wrappers. With two initial pages and a three-page maximum it observed
`2, 2, 3, -1, 3` (size, grow return, size, failed grow return, size).
Sources: pinned third_party/llvm-project/llvm/include/llvm/IR/IntrinsicsWebAssembly.td
and llvm/test/CodeGen/WebAssembly/memory-addr32.ll. memory.size is ordered with
memory.grow, returns 64 KiB pages, and grow returns the previous size or all ones.
These are explicit target foreign bindings, not new portable Foundation operations.
The module is selected only for wasm32; no interpreter/native support is claimed.

Unblocked Wasm work: guest-wasm.tower now connects the existing explicit GuestHeap
to those target operations. It starts an empty arena at the current memory end,
reuses/coalesces committed storage first, grows only on demand, and publishes
limits only after successful growth. Shared request-size rounding lives in
GuestHeap; pointers remain raw. Realloc keeps the old allocation on failure and
copies before releasing it. A full 4 GiB committed memory uses UINT32_MAX as the
arena limit rather than wrapping a one-past pointer to zero, preserving address
overflow policy. Init refuses an already full memory. The owner must serialize
access and exclusively own the suffix; an observed foreign growth prevents
claiming that new range. This is a tested explicit-context replacement component,
not yet the process-wide runtime malloc/free path. runtime.c is retained unchanged
until runtime exports and startup storage can be connected correctly.

Focused tests are Tower sources: allocator-glue.tower exercises real alloc,
realloc/free and all four tower_test_buffer_* functions; allocator-wasm.tower
executes real growth with a 128 KiB initial / 512 KiB maximum memory. The small
Node file only invokes the latter export and reports its status. Isolated
cmake/TowerAllocatorTests.cmake is opt-in via TOWER_ALLOCATOR_TESTS and optionally
TOWER_ALLOCATOR_WASI_SDK. Growth tests link upstream wasi-libc memory routines,
not runtime.c's allocator. Only tower_trap is permitted as an unresolved import.
The WASI libc command entry initially hit undefined_weak:main: Clang normally
rewrites an argc/argv main to __main_argc_argv, while Tower intentionally exports
literal C symbols. allocator-wasi-entry.tower now supplies that documented
upstream startup entry in Tower. No native wrapper or test was written. The
first test compile also caught that `if` takes a simple operand; fixtures now
name their conditions rather than adding expression syntax to Foundation.

Backend-owner blockers, reproduced with the scoped bootstrap and current source:

1. Canonical declarations such as
   `export fn tower_allocate(count: usize, size: usize): void* { return null; }`
   fail with "Function symbol conflicts with Tower runtime". backend_lower also
   creates runtime declarations first and rejects the final foreign symbol, so
   a c_name alias cannot evade this. Required runtime-library signatures are
   tower_allocate(usize,usize):void*, tower_reallocate(void*,usize,usize):void*,
   tower_deallocate(void*):void, tower_print(u32,u64,u32):void and
   tower_trap(u8*,usize):void. They must define/reuse exactly the backend's runtime
   declaration type/calling convention, retain normal Foundation bodies/names
   and canonical round trips, and avoid recursive builtin allocation in their
   implementations. Print's kind/bits/pointer-width ABI and trap message/offset
   must stay unchanged. Guest trap exits with status 1; compiler internal trap
   emits its existing diagnostic and aborts. Wasm guest print/trap imports retain
   module `tower` and their existing import names. This is an explicit runtime
   binding requirement, not permission to rename symbols after code generation.
2. Library `var heap_cursor: usize = 0;` fails with "Library source cannot contain
   top-level executable statements". Runtime heap storage and the existing test
   CompilerMemoryState need ordinary shared global declaration entities, target
   layout and ordered initialization. Zero-initialized storage and any required
   initialization entry must be established before the first allocation. In
   particular fail_after must start at SIZE_MAX, not zero. Preserve the ABI:
   tower_test_buffer_count():usize, tower_test_buffer_allocations():usize,
   tower_test_buffer_fail_next():void, tower_test_buffer_fail_after(usize):void.
   Overflow does not consume an injection/call count; an injected zero-size
   realloc failure precedes deallocation; failure automatically disarms. Existing
   C test-state storage remains, and is intentionally not claimed thread-safe.
3. Proposed Foundation spelling `extern var __heap_base: u8;` is rejected by
   the declaration grammar (extern currently requires fn). Needed semantics:
   imported data entity with ordinary target address `&__heap_base`, linker
   relocation, explicit declared type/layout, no allocation/handle or fabricated
   initialized byte. Wasm's linker supplies the symbol after static data/stack;
   use it to preserve the existing initial heap extent when activating malloc.
   Foreign-data support must use shared nodes and reversible Foundation text.
4. Native startup should use upstream CRT/startup where possible, with Tower
   `export fn main(argc:i32, argv:u8**):i32` calling
   `extern fn tower_main():void`, or the existing Windows mainCRTStartup ABI.
   Referencing tower_main is currently forbidden by the same reserved-name rule.
   Linux freestanding _start also needs ABI-correct initial stack alignment and
   exit; do not replace it with an ordinary C-ABI Tower function on the process
   entry stack. Supply upstream Linux CRT/platform calls in the target pack or
   coordinate an explicit backend entry contract before removing that assembly.
   Existing libc/kernel32 calls cover hosted allocation/output/exit; no speculative
   syscall operation or native fallback was added. Native target-pack integration
   is a remaining dependency, not a deployed all-Tower runtime claim.

## 2026-11-20 — Resolve fields and concrete expressions inside templates

The user's Templates screenshots exposed the next missing layer: hovering
values.count or the subtraction operator inside pop still inherited pop's
function-template presentation. The earlier pass bound declarations and written
annotations, but did not follow dependent type applications into fields or type
body expressions. Describing that pass as partially typed without that boundary
was misleading. A runtime value of values is not needed here: stack(T) always
declares count:usize, while storage.data can remain symbolic as T[4].

Added the bounded Tower-only semantic-generic-values library pass. It follows
original annotation entities with declaration-keyed argument bindings, caches
fixed record shapes on the original constructor components, and attaches member,
index, dereference, assignment and expression information to the original nodes.
All template definitions are bound before this pass, preserving module forward
references. A recognized shape consists of direct struct declarations followed
by a return of one of those structs. Conditional returns and arbitrary type
programs remain unknown; this does not execute type functions speculatively or
select a first concrete instance. Nested substitutions preserve the argument's
own binding context, so differently named parameters and nested integer/type
arguments resolve correctly. Names, field docs and locations refer to their
actual declarations, including imported ones.

Concrete subexpressions reuse sem_expression/sem_operand on temporary clones in
the same entity store, seeded with known operand types. This shares contextual
literal range checks, operation legality, comparison results and target types.
The clones are released, and the original generic body is never partly lowered.
Inference propagates to locals and later lexical uses. Unknown operations now
have their own query components rather than the enclosing function's tooltip.
GenericInfoKind and GenericShapeState use enums; existing inspection limits bound
the analysis. Shared formatting consumes disposable substitution views of the
original nodes; no browser type parser or independent semantic representation
was added. Hover still consumes the existing cached document query.

Refined the previous error-state restriction: unfinished nominal layouts remain
unavailable, but registered primitive field types can be used independently after
an unrelated document error. Thus count and its subtraction still report usize
while incomplete Broken layouts remain suppressed. Ordinary compilation keeps
its diagnostics, and full checking of unused bodies still awaits instantiation.
Substituted composite layouts and arbitrary dependent expression inference are
not implemented by this bounded inspection pass.

Trials/root causes: the new Node tests and actual Templates browser regression
fail against the preceding bundle, with the exact fn pop fallback on both desktop
and mobile. Initial compiler attempts rejected inline binary if conditions and
the reserved identifier expected; changed these to foundation condition locals
and expected_type. A first shape probe found generated optional-capture wrappers
around returns; transparent unnamed single-child relationships now unwrap
generically. Another trial attached formatter substitutions to list wrappers
that the list printer skips; bind the visited type/name/count entities instead.
This also preserves bindings attached to array-count nodes before unwrapping.

Concurrency boundary confirmed in library/entities.tower and compiler/world.tower:
entity_view_query borrows a dense array of component pointers with stable payload
addresses. It is not packed archetype/SoA payload storage or a SIMD guarantee.
The coordinator opens/closes views and changes refcounts; structural mutation
rejects pinned stores. Workers must borrow prepared views and finish before the
coordinator reclaims them. CompilerWorld type creation is lazy, so required kinds
must be resolved before entering a read phase. FrontendCache lookup changes LRU
order/counters, copying changes snapshot references, and pattern reuse updates a
component: these remain coordinator operations. The new emission lookups avoid
all those mutations. Do not describe the current within-unit compiler as fully
parallel; current verified parallelism is independent compiler units/worlds.

## 2026-11-20 - Tower CLI entry and production compiler runtime exports

Agent-2 work in the independent C:/Sandbox/tower-cli-runtime clone on main.
Initial pull was bf906b5; subsequent autostash pulls preserved all local changes
and integrated 0b48236 and 0e4bd41. No parser.cpp, parser-tree-tests.cpp, syntax.cpp,
frontend algorithms, backend lowering, todo.txt, other checkouts or their build
outputs were edited. Sanitizer and whole-repository formatter sweeps remain
intentionally skipped. No additional agents were spawned.

The production main now lives in host/driver-entry.tower. It owns parsed options,
the upstream LLVM C API's default-target string, executable/resource buffers and
timings through the synchronous compiler call and releases them on ordinary
returns. Linux readlink(/proc/self/exe), Darwin _NSGetExecutablePath + realpath,
and Windows GetModuleFileNameA provide resolved executable locations, growing
buffers when necessary. Help/version and malformed-option early exits retain
existing behavior. driver.cpp is now the retained driver_compile transport over
the existing C++ compiler/interpreter interfaces. Its obsolete bootstrap and
interpreter seed branches were deleted, not moved into another native file.
That adapter still owns source/Foundation orchestration, C++ results and existing
process-global syntax_modules; this is not independent concurrent compiler worlds.
Its existing fatal read/abort paths still terminate the process. Do not describe
this entry port as complete retirement of the compiler transport or session state.

Production tower_allocate/tower_reallocate/tower_deallocate and internal trap
reporting now originate in Tower. They reuse host/memory.tower and the shared
platform-output formatter. No new allocator or graph model was introduced.
compiler-memory.cpp contains only the old single-owner test failure-injection
state and its connections. Production builds no longer compile it. The retained
legacy test ABI is not advertised as thread safe; explicit CompilerMemoryState
and CompilerNodeMemoryState callers continue to own their contexts.

The existing backend rejects both literal and foreign-spelled reserved runtime
function definitions. Rather than add a native wrapper or change lowering owned
by another agent, host/runtime-bind.tower uses installed LLVM C APIs to connect
ordinary Tower implementations in emitted target LLVM output. It requires a
defined source function, rejects an already-defined destination and mismatched
function types, replaces declaration uses, removes temporary Wasm export-name
metadata, and verifies the resulting module before writing output. Clang emits
the ordinary target object. This is a private platform artifact step, not a new
Tower program storage format or public instruction ABI. Canonical Foundation
and ordinary reserved-name diagnostics are unchanged. cmake/TowerRuntime.cmake
integrates this step. The binding tool itself links directly to upstream LLVM
and libc without a project-owned runtime seed. Browser packages retain these
small generated runtime ABI objects as prebuilt support while rebuilding host
policies; editing the runtime-object build stage in-browser remains future work.

## 2026-11-20 — Tower surface operators and numeric grammar annotations (in progress)

Request: implement C-style precedence/operators in tower.tower (no arrow), retain
ordinary recursive grammar chaining and associativity, use shared ECS semantics,
and audit Tower-importing code for simplifications and hardcoded constants.
Started with git pull --rebase on main: 5b77c88 -> bf906b5, clean checkout.
Foundation remains unchanged. Bedrock adds only general optional production
metadata: `@ <positive u32> left|right|nonassoc`, with `L>R` / `R<L` aliases.
Annotations live on SyntaxNode alternatives and parser-rule entities; LR records
are disposable derived data. The formatter and structural equality include them.
Only explicitly annotated shift/reduce pairs are resolved. Unannotated conflicts
and reduce/reduce conflicts retain diagnostics. Nonassoc removes the conflicting
terminal action. Associativity does not authorize algebraic reassociation.

The first spelling used literal left/right keywords and broke existing capture
names ($left) because literals become lexical keywords. Replaced the direction
with a contextual token and chose @ for the annotation delimiter. Mixed literal
L>R is also outside the existing literal category policy; a contextual token
preserves the requested compact aliases without changing that policy.

Surface operators augment the existing entities during checking, then normalize
into Foundation locals, calls, binary operations, addresses, loads/stores, loops
and branches before backend consumption. Temporary surface classifications have
no execution-cache encoding. Calls/operands retain left-to-right value capture;
assignment addresses and compound-assignment old values are captured before RHS
effects. Short-circuit and conditional RHS work stays inside selected branches.
Prefix/postfix ++/-- cover integer/pointer places, including indexed places.
Shifts currently expand portably into Foundation arithmetic: count modulo width,
wrapping left shifts and sign-extending signed right shifts. This explicit Tower
policy avoids inheriting host/C undefined behavior for excessive/negative counts.
Three-way comparison produces i32 -1/0/1. Existing convert/bits/sizeof/alignof and
alloc/free remain ordinary calls; no C++ object model, exceptions or arrow is added.

Trials: a graph-only smoke passed arithmetic, !, ~, increments and shifts. A
larger trace covering short-circuit effects, ternaries, chained assignment,
indexed updates, pointer loads, shifts and signed minimums matches graph execution,
fast execution of reconstructed Foundation, and native LLVM executable output.
A round-trip trial exposed generated &*pointer, which Foundation cannot spell;
address-of-load and indirect assignment now reuse the already captured pointer.
A return trial exposed its optional capture wrapper; restored the existing outer
CoreOperand collection before checking its nested surface expression.

Signed literal clarification: Number still excludes a sign. Typing reads an exact

Added C#-inspired `??`, `??=`, `?.`, `?[]`, `is null`, `is not null`, `>>>` and

operator classification and assignment lowering. Their destinations are evaluated
once, and logical/null RHS work stays inside the selected branch. Guarded scalar
access currently requires a consuming `??`; first-class nullable scalar storage
is not implemented. Guarded pointer results can remain nullable pointers. Nested
fields/indexing preserve this guard and skip index effects on missing receivers.
Separate canonical projection nodes avoid a cycle when rewriting guarded source
nodes to their results. Foundation reconstruction also caught `(*p).field` and
dereferenced-array places: normalize these to Foundation's indirect field/index
spellings before formatting.

research entries retain their original paths as historical evidence. AGENTS.md
now records the naming and import contract. No todo.txt edits were made; its
pre-existing edits and later concurrent changes remain user-owned.

`foo.bar` selects foo/bar.tower, `.foo.bar` selects ../foo/bar.tower, and every
additional leading dot adds another parent. Prefix imports never search libraries.
Bedrock's existing ImportPath retains identifier segments and `previous`; a new
ImportName wraps that path or a `parent` prefix. The immutable Tower-built seed
and parsed Bedrock use the same rules. Prefix terms live on their actual syntax
entities, alongside identifier terms, and the shared formatter emits both.
Validation requires the declaration reader's captures. Cache re-resolution now
retains the quoted/unquoted distinction as part of the import declaration.

Quoted paths are complete filenames, with no implicit extension or builtin-name
alias. Arbitrary user directory names, hyphens, spaces, extensionless source files
and other extensions remain supported. Browser source capabilities now transport
all supplied text files so an explicit filename is not filtered by `.tower`.
These are still Tower source imports, not a new PNG/binary-asset loader.

Native case checking is Tower code. Platform implementations use Linux/Darwin
directory entries and Windows CRT `_findfirst64`; WASI source/file keys already
compare exactly. Checks reject incorrect directory/basename/extension case and
Windows short-name/trailing-dot aliases. A mismatched nearer filename cannot hide
a correctly spelled library candidate. Linux/Darwin ABI profiles are explicit
x86_64/AArch64 layouts; macOS execution has not been tested here. POSIX checking
requires directory enumeration permission. Drive-letter normalization and UNC
server/share root lookup retain their platform policy. Sources for these ABIs:
[Linux readdir](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/readdir.3.html),
[Microsoft file-search functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/filename-search-functions?view=msvc-170).

Symlink and hard-link identity remains lexical. File reads follow symlinks, but
two lexical aliases can repeat initialization. Lexical `..` is normalized before
filesystem traversal and does not follow a symlink's physical parent. Symlink
cycles may hit the depth limit. These limitations are documented rather than
silently introducing a host-dependent realpath identity policy.

Browser compiler project refresh retires obsolete unchanged bundled paths while
preserving edited/user files. Old edited modules are retained for manual migration;
their old quoted spelling is not silently reinterpreted. The source naming audit
now has a regression test, as does this project refresh behavior.

Environment: Windows PowerShell, Node 21.7.3, WSL Orchestral-Revng, LLVM 19,
Clang 19 (installed for the upstream runtime binding step), WASI SDK 34 and the
existing pinned LLVM/WASI cache. The starting pull fast-forwarded 7ecd752 to
451cc14 with autostash, preserving existing AGENTS/docs/journal/todo work. Git's
automatic geometric repack stalled that pull; stopping the optional pack process

The private transport supplies source files, not a second import resolver. LLVM

https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/sys/stat.h and

Implementation is entirely Tower: grammar in tower.tower, checking/lowering in
semantic_control.tower with ordinary Foundation blocks, locals, branches, stores

When the body's control-flow summary contains a reachable continue, a first-entry
flag moves the single update to the next loop head; ordinary loops append it after
the body. This avoids duplicating the update or changing nested continues. No
runtime speed claim is made. A trapping initializer preserves definite-return
analysis. For lowering enforces the existing 128-level Foundation block ceiling.

### 2026-11-20 � Agent 3: retire native byte-buffer and UTF-8 test drivers

Assignment: migrate native parser/ECS functional coverage to executable Tower,
keeping reference oracles and allocation/lifetime assertions. This first slice
replaces `tests/bytes.cpp` and `tests/utf8.cpp` with Tower tests and an isolated
`cmake/TowerUtilityTests.cmake`; production implementations are unchanged.

The byte suite preserves the original xorshift seed, seven operations and 20,000
trials, reference success/capacity/full-allocation-byte comparison, guard checks,
failure atomicity, guaranteed moving growth, self-alias rebasing, terminator and
size overflow rejection, ABI offsets and final empty allocation registry. The
reference callback ABI has no context argument, so this single-process test owns
explicitly initialized module state and a bounded eight-slot allocation registry
(at most three buffers are live during a move). Snapshot memory uses libc directly
and is released. This is test instrumentation, not Foundation pointer semantics.

UTF-8 preserves every scalar through U+110000, surrogate/out-of-range rejection,
all one/two-byte strings, 100,000 seeded mixed inputs, policy values 0/1/42,
unchanged short destinations, and Linux/macOS inaccessible-page read/write
boundaries. The original RNG state continues into the boundary trials. Existing
native seeds are retained as differential oracles, not production fallbacks.

### 2026-11-20 - Tower-owned session input leases (agent 1, next slice)

While the coordinator holds the combined-publication lock, moved the next bounded
ownership unit into syntax_session_inputs.tower: source snapshots, declaration
documents, owned versus borrowed module leases, and reset/disposal. The native
SyntaxSession now embeds the plain ABI view and calls Tower operations; its
set_source implementation and native source/document ownership are removed.
The environment/world are explicit borrowed inputs. Module construction still
uses its existing host-world API; this does not claim arbitrary-world module
parsing, complete SyntaxSession retirement or within-unit concurrency.

Reset prepares a source snapshot and shared-entity declaration document before
publishing them. Failure in either preparation retains the prior owned inputs;
the native caller clears its executable version and reports the error. A retry
still rebuilds an owned module graph instead of reusing its recorded declarations.
Replacing an owned module with a supplied borrowed module releases the owned graph
and keeps the supplied graph alive after session disposal. Template readers use
the same source snapshot operation. Existing source/tree pins survive the owner.

New Tower tests exercise length-delimited snapshot text, Bedrock/Foundation/user
source names, every source/document preparation allocation failure, pinned-view
reset rejection, source-only template replacement, retained-source/document
lifetimes after owner disposal, idempotent disposal, owned module reset after
failure, and owned-to-borrowed module transition. The initial frontend abort was
in the test's final host-world allocation-count assertion: warming only a module
had not warmed the persistent syntax-component storage used by documents. Warming
a complete owner before that baseline makes the same lifetime check pass; explicit
world tests still require complete disposal back to their original buffer count.
Temporary print tracing first failed to link because this focused library target
does not link tower_print. Used temporary libc puts/fflush to locate the assertion,
then removed all tracing and reran. No new native tests or implementation were added.

Current default-pin native build succeeds; anchored frontend/driver checks pass
2/2 (16.95 s), including the new tests. The actual compiler passes module_paths.py.
Logs: C:/Sandbox/build/codex-agents/agent-1-session-inputs-{build,module-paths}.log.
This slice remains local until the coordinator completes the current publication;
a fresh clean successor after its final source rebase is still required.

Verified source findings at 479962b:

- `tower.tower` supplies expressions, precedence and compounds. Existing local
  inference, enums, match/while, vectors/stack/queue and type/integer specialization
  should not be proposed as unimplemented. The roadmap ledger and Tower guide
  still described expressions as pending; corrected those statements, including
  the old no-comma proposal. Implementation and hosted publication remain distinct.
- `semantic_layout.tower` uses work_request/depend/seal/demand but invokes each
  sem_layout_compute synchronously inside work_take. No work_access declarations
  occur in compiler semantic kernels. Pinned EntityView protects structure and
  lifetime, not arbitrary payload writes. This confirms the remembered within-unit
  limitation; the issue is not an absent unit-level worker transport.
- `semantic_statements.tower::sem_run` still iterates global phases and function
  bodies with one mutable SemanticContext. `sem_declaration_type` has a separate
  recursive inference chain/128-entry guard. Shared scope, error state, generic
  tables and scratch cannot simply be used by concurrent kernels.
- `work_graph.tower::work_depend` permits new edges only for a Building consumer.
  It is a useful predeclared dependency scheduler, not yet a suspend/discover/resume
  engine for running staged code. Layout's graph uses revision 1 and pointer width
  as its profile for one compilation; this is not full persistent invalidation.
- `compiler_work.tower` creates independent Unit tasks and one Join. Browser/Node
  workers compile each unit's import closure in isolated instances. It does not
  deduplicate or schedule declaration-level queries across those units. Native
  CLI worker pools and shared-world phase dispatch are still pending.
- `SemanticTypeUse` records resolved types on the original shared entities for
  opt-in inspection. It is a useful component path, not an implemented decltype
  operator or arbitrary first-class type execution.
- `generic_type_result` recognizes an optional struct plus return; other statements
  explicitly diagnose missing general compile-time execution. sem_constant_argument
  accepts integer literals or bound values. `const Name()` is still an ordinary
  function, not a compile-time evaluator or memoization guarantee.
- `interpreter_init` begins at the program root. Ordinary function frames and
  resumable steps exist, but staging needs an explicit invocation/result context,
  dependency suspension and a strict effect/memory policy. Foundation docs explicitly
  exclude invalid/uninitialized raw accesses from the current differential contract;
  the ordinary interpreter is not automatically a strict compile-time environment.

Recommended scoped implementation, recorded in docs/tower-language-plan.md:
unevaluated decltype using ordinary semantic types; shared binding/type/signature/
body/layout/evaluation queries with coordinator-owned suspension and actual cycle
paths; a real dependency-ready within-unit layout batch consumer; then pure ordinary
integer/bool function execution via the existing interpreter and typed Foundation
constant materialization. Strict initialized-read checks, transitive effect gating,
explicit target/profile/fuel and no execution of unrelated module initializers are
part of that slice. Follow with executable first-class type values, arbitrary owned
values/graphs/functions and tracked I/O. Do not add another evaluator or public IR.
General type construction cannot be claimed merely because scalar comptime works.

Declare read/write ranges, pin inputs, isolate scratch/results, and publish shared
components deterministically before releasing consumers. Cache keys and dependency
reads include module/world/revision, arguments, target/semantics and effects; use
stable identities for cross-instance reuse. Preserve lexical visibility, ordered
module effects and incremental grammar activation. Test one large unit, many
modules in one unit, and multiple units sharing a dependency diamond; observe
real within-unit overlap separately from unit-worker or synthetic SIMD results.
for/foreach implementation remains with its existing owner.

Implemented the first scheduler prerequisite in library/work_graph.tower:
coordinator-owned work_suspend adds a discovered dependency, releases the execution
lease, seals/recounts its remaining inputs and demands the dependency. Every
dispatch now has a generation in WorkTicket; stale results cannot finish or suspend
a later dispatch of the same query. Compiler unit receipts explicitly use their
single dispatch generation. The new Tower work_resume fixture checks lazy unused
work, lease release, shared-input deduplication, repeated completed dependencies,
old receipts after resume, failed inputs, cancellation and dynamic/self cycle paths.
Its native graph and optimized fast runs both print zero. The first fixture compile
correctly rejected a missing direct vector import; fixed the import rather than
weakening module visibility.

Started a Tower-only interpreter context refactor. IMExecution carries the existing
IMState pointer plus an optional owned IMContext. Existing runtime/fast entry points
wrap the same operation handlers with their original signatures; the native state
layout and C++ sources are unchanged. Explicit invocation starts a selected checked
function with supplied arguments, rather than entering all module initialization.
The context owns results/errors, target width, strict-mode initialization metadata
and deterministic fuel. Unsupported storage/global/output/foreign effects are gated
in strict mode; arithmetic still uses the original runtime operation implementation.
This is initial scalar-stage infrastructure, not completed source comptime, type
values or dependency integration. The first compatibility-context native rebuild
passed; invocation/strict-mode rebuild and dedicated tests remain in progress.

Layout integration now prepares per-type pending-result components on the same

passes discover all pending types before dispatch so independent types within one
unit can run concurrently. A context retains its pool across layout requests.
This integration is being built/tested; do not yet claim it passed. The first native

Layouts and evaluations now share SemanticContext.queries. Evaluation requests,

### Compiler-wide threading is a primary objective; parser specialization is future guidance

The user clarified during this continuation that migration of the **entire
compiler** to ECS and threaded execution is a primary objective alongside
`decltype` and compile-time execution. Completion of a staged evaluator alone
must not be reported as completion of this work. Continue replacing serial
compiler paths with shared entity/component queries, declared accesses,
worker-owned results and deterministic publication. Dense archetype/column access
and stable sparse components are complementary storage choices; select them for
actual access and lifetime requirements, rather than changing semantic identity
or introducing a second compiler graph. Structural publication, ordered grammar
updates and effects can require sequencing; that is not permission to leave
independent expensive work serialized. The singleton host world, semantic body
checking/lowering, parser sessions/caches and backend/context ownership remain
explicit migration items.

The following is **future direction supplied by the user, not a request to
implement parser specialization or JSON benchmarking now**:

- Parse grammars, DFA/LR tables, precedence helpers and related compiler data
  should eventually be usable as compile-time values through ordinary Tower
  compiler services/imports. Explicitly tracked compile-time file reads should
  permit constructing those values by interpreting ordinary Tower code first.
- Freeze eligible results into a build so optimization sees their contents.
  Explore specializing the ordinary parser against that constant grammar,
  including direct Foundation/LLVM generation where useful. Ship prebuilt parser
  and compiler implementations with distribution binaries; avoid rebuilding the
  compiler's own unchanged grammar at every launch.
- Start execution early through the graph or fast interpreter. Where supported,
  compile a replacement implementation for native CPU or browser Wasm, validate
  it, and switch at a safe boundary. Keep interpretation available on platforms
  that cannot load generated native code. Runtime grammar edits should produce a
  new dependency/version identity and optionally a new compiled implementation.
- Explore caching compiled artifacts or code pages, subject to target, semantics,
  dependency, relocation and lifetime contracts. A cached execution artifact is
  derived data, never a second authoritative program format. Canonical Foundation
  remains the semantic interchange and reconstruction source.
- A future end-to-end experiment should implement a conformant JSON parser in
  Tower grammar, import/use it through compiler services or ordinary Tower code,
  and compare against established fast JSON parsers. Define correctness, Unicode,
  malformed-input behavior, API/output allocation and benchmark conditions before
  interpreting speed differences. No claim that Tower is already faster.
- The motivating developer experience resembles editable game database values
  that become generated constants in release builds: one ordinary data/program
  model with explicit dynamic versus frozen inputs, giving optimizers useful
  information without requiring users to maintain a separate code generator.

Clarification to preserve when implementing that future work: knowing the
**grammar/table contents** at compile time does not make an unknown input stream's
characters constant. It enables specialization of the parser's fixed decisions;
input-dependent transitions remain runtime work. Inlining and constant folding
may remove substantial indirection, but do not by themselves guarantee an optimal
DFA, complete table-to-code conversion or fastest-possible machine code. Compare
ordinary constant-data optimization with deliberate specialization, code-size and
instruction-cache costs, and retain equivalent interpreted behavior. The current
scalar staging implementation is not yet frozen aggregate/file-input support;
that remains a required architectural extension, not a capability verified here.

### Shared-memory worker transport and declaration graph continuation

Pulled/rebased onto `60dfb51`, retaining upstream parser pending-name/precedence
and browser fixes. The journal-only autostash conflict was resolved by retaining
the complete upstream journal plus this work's appended entries; no TODO edits.
The 11-test compile-time group passed before the header-graph expansion, including
both pointer widths, Foundation reconstruction, interpreter behavior, LLVM output,
invalid staged effects/lifetimes/fuel/cycles and two 1,024-entry forward type chains
(`build/language-next-audit/declaration-tests.log`).

Added an experimental WASI Preview 1 threads transport entirely in Tower for
pthread/semaphore operations. JavaScript supplies Web Workers and shared memory;
Tower continues to own kernels, work admission, dependencies and publication.
The transport uses wasi-sdk 34's threaded libc for stacks, TLS and allocator
synchronization. Secondary instances call `wasi_thread_start`, never `_initialize`;
wasm-ld's synchronized shared-memory initialization prevents data reset. The
callback occupies a matching appended indirect-table slot in each instance.
References: the [WASI threads ABI](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasi-threads)
and [WASI SDK](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasi-sdk/blob/main/README.md).
This is an explicit supported transport profile, not a requirement that portable
interpretation allocate executable memory.

Trials and corrections: SDK 34's legacy `wasi-sdk-pthread.cmake` selects the old
`wasm32-wasi-threads` spelling while this package installs
`wasm32-wasip1-threads`; the first configure therefore could not find crt/libc.
`cmake/WasiThreads.cmake` selects the installed target and propagates its SDK path
through CMake compiler checks. The first host instantiation lacked the advisory
WASI `sched_yield` import; added that host operation. A standalone test link that
explicitly exported `main` pulled an additional libc main adapter and produced a
duplicate Wasm export; rely on the Tower export metadata instead.

The first real Chromium barrier trial timed out although the same Wasm binary
passed in Node. Network/worker tracing showed nested workers requested but not

completion flag allows reuse without needing a parent message callback while
Wasm is blocked. Chromium then passed the four-worker barrier. Its next trial
caught a separate browser ABI issue: TextDecoder rejects SharedArrayBuffer views.
Host text decoding now copies shared views at the published-result boundary;
ordinary ArrayBuffer paths retain their existing behavior. A harness-only trial
also supplied the Foundation argument in the wrong loader slot and was corrected.

With these corrections, real headless Chromium under explicit COOP/COEP headers

### Continuation: compiled regex guidance and a real shared-memory failure

The user clarified the future specialization example: ordinary Tower code should
compile a constant regex into a DFA, expose the resulting immutable transitions
and character classes to specialization, and eventually produce tight native
matching code. The input characters are still runtime values. A constant table
permits folding and specialization but does not guarantee that LLVM eliminates
every lookup or discovers an optimal branch layout; explicit staged construction
of Foundation code may be useful too. Keep one semantic graph, compile-time/runtime
operation contracts, target/profile identity and interpreter fallback. This remains
future guidance, alongside the parser/JSON examples, not an instruction to start
regex code generation during the ECS/decltype/compile-time dependency work.

The LR regression run exposed a real intermittent failure, distinct from the
previous slow module-suite investigation. Individual test files passed, and one
combined repetition passed 21/21 in 12.35 s, but other combined runs timed out.
Node 21.7.3 inspector sampling of an owned stalled test process showed the root in
work_signal_wait from lr_states_lalr_parallel during bootstrap grammar setup.
NodeWorker inspector sessions showed three workers waiting for jobs, one idle,
and shared status [2,2,3,2]: the idle worker had failed. Capturing its exception
identified memory.fill in memset, called by lr_kernel_closure immediately after
allocating its 68-byte result. Relinking the same objects without --strip-all and
llvm-objdump-19 located that exact fill; libc's dlmalloc/realloc do contain locks.
The root could not receive the queued JS error while synchronously waiting for a
completion semaphore, so the failure appeared as a deadlock. This is not evidence
that the compile-time dependency graph itself cycles or loses a task.

The observed trap is consistent with a known V8 shared-memory growth defect:
other workers can use a stale bound until servicing an engine interrupt. The
upstream [V8 fix](https://github.com/v8/v8/commit/34241014663390c72e08c123faef6fedf395be8e)
changes shared memory.size and bounds checks to read the backing store length.
The [napi-rs WASI documentation](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs/blob/main/cli/docs/wasi.md#shared-memory-growth-on-wasm32-wasip1-threads)
documents allocator synchronization and worker-handoff refresh as compatibility
measures. This research explains a concrete candidate root cause; the new
compatibility path still needs controlled stress validation before calling it fixed.

Added Tower host wrappers around the shared-WASI libc allocation entry points,
with platform-only JS atomic lock/memory-view refresh primitives, and a refresh
at semaphore handoff. Native allocator behavior remains its platform libc. No new
C++ was added. The wrapper covers zero fill and realloc copying as well as malloc,
and serializes growth with refresh before allocator entry. Separately, worker
errors now publish bounded UTF-8 reports through shared state. Tower semaphore
waits check that state with a 100 ms timed wait, so a guest trap can interrupt the
blocked coordinator without waiting for its JS event loop. Fatal instances are
abandoned; freeing through an allocator potentially interrupted in another thread
is unsafe. An initial timed-wait trial incorrectly passed integer zero to WASI
clock_gettime: SDK 34 uses a pointer-valued clockid_t. Removed that assumption and
use an explicit host clock primitive solely for scheduler deadlines, never as a
compile-time program input. The actual sem_timedwait timespec layout and errno
values were checked against the installed SDK headers.

both compositions. The pool fixture now also exercises concurrent allocation,
